correctness.rationale: Re-derived the two Taylor cases from the actual RESULT.md. If the first nonharmonic homogeneous term has degree k<2m, the first mean defect is -pk/(n+k) times its strictly positive spherical mean; positivity follows because the leading nonzero homogeneous term of Δv≥0 is nonnegative. If all lower terms are harmonic, the degree-2m defect is -2mp/(n+2m)⟨P_2m⟩ + p/2(pn/(n+2m)-1)⟨P_m²⟩. The first summand is nonpositive, the second strictly negative below p=1+2m/n. The C^{2m} Taylor remainder suffices. Taking v=H_m homogeneous harmonic makes the coefficient positive above this threshold. The m=1 coefficient algebraically matches Mochizuki's published Pizzetti coefficient.
